title: arXiv physics daily — 2026-11-26 announcement batch: 9 notable recent papers
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart. This inferred ordering uses only cross-list counts for the selected records because no measured external engagement was present and Semantic Scholar citation data was unavailable; it is a notable-paper list, not a popularity ranking.

sections.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
sections.abstract: The authors prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis transverse spin-gradient approximation to noncollinear spin density functional theory using a spin-spiral reference.
sections.claimed_result: Csirik proves an O(N^(5/6)) error for an energy of order N under stated slow-variation and regularity assumptions, and recovers the noncollinear local spin-density approximation when the spiral phase is set to zero.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; analytic bound for the thermodynamic-limit electron gas with a spin-spiral-wave local reference.
sections.unique_caveat: The bound is for a fixed-axis variant and depends on smooth, slowly varying rotating-frame density and local wavevector; it is not an empirical accuracy benchmark for general materials.

sections.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
sections.abstract: The authors prove that the asymptotic expansion of the figure-eight knot's colored Jones polynomial is connected to non-perturbative topological recursion on its elliptic spectral curve.
sections.claimed_result: Hock and Shadrin identify the asymptotic Jones-polynomial wave function with the recurrence and normalized non-perturbative wave functions for the figure-eight-knot spectral curve, proving the proposed connection in this case.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; analysis of the colored-Jones recurrence, spectral curve, and topological-recursion equations.
sections.unique_caveat: The proof is specific to the figure-eight knot and the colored Jones polynomial; extension to other knots is posed as a follow-up question, not established here.

sections.title: Noise-induced Extinction in Hierarchical Food Webs
sections.abstract: The authors develop a large-deviation account of demographic-noise-driven extinctions in hierarchical food webs, deriving an extinction network and recursion for mean extinction times.
sections.claimed_result: Under unit conversion efficiency and self-limitation only at the basal species, the authors show coexistence is the sole stable mean-field state and derive a 3^(N−1)-transition extinction network; their three-species instanton route is checked against stochastic simulations.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical and computational; WKB analysis of the master equation, numerical instantons for a three-species omnivory model, and stochastic simulations.
sections.unique_caveat: The general results rely on an idealized hierarchical interaction structure and restrictive ecological assumptions; direct simulation checks cover the three-species example, not arbitrary food webs.

sections.title: Unified preparation of exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scars from Dicke states
sections.abstract: The authors propose a unified algorithm that prepares exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scar states by mapping them to Dicke states and ferromagnetic-chain magnons.
sections.claimed_result: Asari, Kunimi, and Nikuni show that at fixed target fidelity the block-encoding success probability has a positive lower bound independent of system size and scar index, so only a constant number of amplitude-amplification rounds is needed.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; quantum-algorithm construction and resource analysis for three scar models.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an algorithmic proposal for idealized programmable simulators; the abstract does not demonstrate preparation on hardware or quantify noise and gate costs.

sections.title: PINN-Slicer: Exploiting Rotational Symmetry to Solve the Photon Orbit Equation Around a Black Hole
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a slice-by-slice physics-informed neural-network method for long-domain autonomous ODEs and demonstrate it on the photon-orbit equation around a black hole.
sections.claimed_result: David, Oepeng, and Prosper report pointwise RMSE below 10^-3 in inverse radius relative to a finite-difference reference, with one trained network generalizing across initial conditions in its training range; the arXiv comment notes code availability and workshop acceptance.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; a PINN benchmarked against a finite-difference solution of the Schwarzschild photon-orbit ODE.
sections.unique_caveat: The validation is one ODE problem and uses a numerical reference solution; generalization beyond the trained initial-condition range and to other physical systems remains untested in the abstract.

sections.title: Moon Radio Interferometer for Science and Exploration (MoonRISE): A Mission Concept for a Low-Frequency Radio Interferometer on the Lunar Farside
sections.authors_display: Saptarshi Bandyopadhyay, Marin Anderson, Alexander Hegedus, Kalind Carpenter, Jack Burns, et al.
sections.abstract: The authors present MoonRISE, a proposed lunar-farside, all-sky radio interferometer operating from 100 kHz to 30 MHz, with heliophysics, lunar-ionosphere, and planetary-radio science goals.
sections.claimed_result: Bandyopadhyay et al. describe a nine-dipole, 1.5-km optical-fibre-tether concept intended to measure type-III burst scattering, the lunar ionosphere, and Uranian kilometric radiation if the mission is realized.
sections.evidence_type: Forecast/proposal; mission and payload concept, not an operating instrument or observational result.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed science depends on mission selection, deployment, radio-frequency cleanliness, and technology maturity; none is demonstrated by this concept paper.

sections.title: Quantum Noise-Limited Terahertz Interferometry for Distinguishing Ultra-Compact Supermassive Galactic Objects
sections.abstract: The authors model whether high-sensitivity terahertz interferometric visibilities could distinguish a Schwarzschild black hole from a JMN-1 naked-singularity model for Sgr A*.
sections.claimed_result: For optically thin spherical accretion onto Sgr A*, Patel et al. calculate separable visibility windows at specified baselines and flux errors, about 28 times below the 2017 EHT statistical uncertainty, and argue that minutes-long coherent integration would be needed.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; modeled gravitational-lensing images and interferometric visibilities under an accretion and noise model.
sections.unique_caveat: The discrimination forecast depends on spherical, optically thin accretion and demanding sensitivity assumptions; it is not an observation of a naked singularity or evidence against an event horizon.

sections.title: Infrared-absorption magnetometry in a diamond nanocavity: demonstration and limits at the nanoscale
sections.authors_display: Nicholas J. Sorensen, Elham Zohari, Chris Coutts, Sean McNaney, Matteo Feder, et al.
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate cavity-enhanced magnetometry by measuring spin-dependent infrared absorption at the NV-centre singlet transition in a spin-dense diamond nanocavity.
sections.claimed_result: Sorensen et al. observe spin-dependent cavity transmission near 1042 nm, demonstrate cavity-enhanced magnetic-field sensing, and experimentally validate a model of the cavity response.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; spin-dense diamond nanocavities probing the NV singlet transition, with a validated response model.
sections.unique_caveat: This establishes a readout method in the demonstrated nanocavity configuration, not a deployed sensor network or a general sensitivity advantage across all sensor geometries.

sections.title: Chiral Domain-Wall Modes in Topological Adaptive Quantum Dynamics
sections.abstract: The authors study measurement-and-feedback adaptive circuits and find chiral dynamical topological domain-wall modes with long-time scaling consistent with a chiral free-fermion conformal field theory.
sections.claimed_result: Bhuiyan, Pan, and Jian report chiral modes localized at domain walls in a 2+1D charge-conserving free-fermion adaptive-circuit model, with logarithmic entanglement and charge-variance scaling and algebraically decaying density correlations.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; free-fermion circuit model with measurement, feedforward, and quantum-trajectory analysis.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is established in a specific free-fermion model; robustness to interactions, hardware noise, and experimental implementation is not shown.
